text: Oh fantastic, my 'friend' posted the embarrassing photo after I begged her not to. Truly a gift.
Love how the landlord 'fixed' the boiler by turning it off and on. Fourth cold shower this week. Living the dream.
Great to hear in the all-hands that 'we're a family here' right before they announced the layoffs.
So nice of Gavin to reply-all with my mistake to the entire company. What a team player.
Wonderful. The council fined me for parking in my own street because the sign changed overnight. Brilliant system.
Oh sure, Dad, I'll 'just get a proper job'. Thanks for that insight at my own birthday dinner.
Delighted that the airline charged me £60 for a bag they then lost. Superb value.
Fantastic news: the insurance won't cover the flood because it was 'surface water'. As opposed to what, sky water?
Ah yes, another 5am wake-up from the toddler. My favourite time of day.
Loving this fourth night of insomnia. Really refreshing.
What a relaxing holiday: three flights, two delays, one lost passport and zero sleep.
Nothing says self-care like working through lunch for the eleventh day running.
Brilliant weekend of 'rest': cleaned the house, did the shopping, drove the kids to four parties.
Perfect, the software update deleted my settings. Again. Thanks so much.
Oh good, another meeting that could have been an email. Can't get enough of those.
Absolutely love being put on hold for 45 minutes to be told to 'check the website'.
Great, my 'quick' tax return has now taken three evenings. Very quick indeed.
Superb timing from the washing machine, dying on the day the in-laws arrive.
Thrilled to discover the 'shortcut' Asif recommended added forty minutes to the drive.
Lovely birthday. Everyone forgot. Even the bakery forgot my order. Truly memorable.
Yay, another wedding where I'm the only single one at the table. So much fun answering questions about it.
Great, the job I really wanted went to the boss's nephew. Life is so fair.
Oh brilliant, three deadlines on the same day. Who doesn't love a challenge.
Really enjoying juggling the move, the new job and a sick dog all in one week. Highly recommend.
Fun times: forty unread emails, six missed calls and a calendar that looks like a game of Tetris.
Super fun Saturday night with my best friend, Netflix. Again.
So great having 800 followers and nobody to call when the car broke down.
Wonderful being the friend everyone forgets until they need a lift to the airport.
Set one place at the table. Opened one beer. Turned on the match and talked to the telly.
Phone in my hand all evening, scrolling through contacts, not pressing any of them.
Walked through the park and every bench had two people on it.
Talked to the barista for longer than strictly necessary. Then the man at the post office. Then the cat.
Booked a table for one at the restaurant and the waiter took the other chair away.
Feet up, a pot of tea, the garden doing its thing outside the window. Wouldn't swap it.
The bills are paid, the fridge is full and the kids are laughing upstairs. That'll do.
Same café, same seat, same flat white, same nod from the owner. I love my little rut.
Dinner with the old crowd. Nobody looked at their phone. Walked home humming.
Clean sheets, open window, a book I'm halfway through. Not asking for anything else today.
Shoulders down for the first time all week. Long exhale on the doorstep.
Let the phone ring out. Finished my tea. The world kept turning.
Watched the rain run down the window for twenty minutes and didn't think about a single thing.
Breathing slowed, heartbeat slowed, the decision made itself.
Already packed. The trip is in nine days.
Checked the tracking number eleven times today. The parcel is in Leicester. Getting closer.
Made a playlist for the road trip. It's four hours long. The trip is three.
Couldn't sit still at work. Kept opening the venue website to look at the stage.
Bought a guidebook, a phrasebook and a tiny umbrella. The flights are in March.
Planted the apple tree for whoever lives here in twenty years.
Put my name down for the course starting in September. Bought the textbook already.
Wrote the CV. Sent four applications. Ironed the interview shirt just in case.
Taped the scan photo to the fridge. Bought one tiny pair of socks. Not tempting fate further.
The rescue dog took a treat from my hand today instead of from the floor.
Wrote Mrs. Lindgren a card for every Christmas for ten years. Today I finally told her why.
Saved the voicemail from the surgeon who caught it early. Listen to it sometimes.
Paid for the stranger's groceries in front of me, like someone once did for me.
Kept the note Dimitri slipped under my door in the worst week. Folded it into my wallet.
Pinned the certificate above my desk where I can see it every morning.
Showed Mum the article with my name in it. Read it to her twice.
Wore the medal to the pub. Didn't take it off all evening.
Hung the painting I made in the hall where visitors see it first.
Checked the door lock three times and the oven twice before I could sleep.
Rehearsed what I'm going to say to the consultant out loud in the car. Twelve times.
Bit my nails down to nothing waiting for the email.
Wrote a list of lists. Then lost it. Then cried in the stationery aisle.
Opened the laptop, stared at the inbox, closed it again, sat in the car for twenty minutes.
Forgot to eat, forgot the dentist, forgot it was Tuesday.
Kept turning the old photo over in my hands. Same face, different person.
Sat on the bench outside my old school for a while and didn't go in.
Left his toothbrush where it was. It's been six months.
Made his favourite tea out of habit and then poured it down the sink.
